payload.rebuttal: argued: The spec requires exactly this: no fallback to an older waiting row, for any state the newest task holds, not only MERGED/REJECTED. The 'newest task decides first' section says the resolver 'stacks on no row, even an older one it would otherwise take' when the newest is MERGED or REJECTED, and the 'wrong versions' list separately and unconditionally names 'a resolver that falls back to an older waiting row' as a bug the witnesses must catch, with no carve-out for DRAFT, QUEUED, ORPHANED, or any other state. Narrowing the no-fallback rule to only MERGED/REJECTED would itself be the forbidden fallback resolver for every other non-accepted state, and would fail the hidden wrong-version check the task names. The scenario the finding describes, a parent with a genuinely waiting older row and an unrelated newer row sitting in some other state, is the same concurrency case the spec's own 'Out of scope' section defers to backlog item 29 ('the resumed-task window'), so handling it specially here is out of scope by the spec's own words, not an oversight. I did fix the comment at that line, though, since it described the rule as if it applied only to merged or closed parents, when the code and the spec apply it to every non-accepted state alike.
